title: Sorting search results only reorders the top-N relevance hits, and Date Created / Last Opened / Permissions are blank for results
problem: Two defects make Sort By unreliable in results. (1) The engine ranks by relevance and truncates to the limit (`raw.sort_by_key(score)` ... `raw.truncate(limit)`, crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs:584-587); the request carries no sort (src/finder/mod.rs:1380-1387) and `set_sort` while searching only sets `result_sort` and re-sorts the rows already fetched (mod.rs:2146-2157, 1222-1259). With more matches than `result_limit` (500), 'Sort by Size' or 'Date Modified' shows the biggest/newest of an arbitrary relevance-ranked 500, not of all matches, so the file you are sorting for can be missing with no hint. (2) File hits are built from the index with `created: None, mode: None, last_opened: None` (engine.rs:1384-1397). The Sort By menu still offers Date Created while searching (src/finder/toolbar.rs:551-556), and the comparator is `a.created.cmp(&b.created)` / `a.last_opened.cmp(...)` (crates/fffinder-core/src/listing.rs:182-183): every file ties, so the result is a name sort with folder hits (stat'ed in `into_hit`) lumped at one end. The Date Created and Date Last Opened columns are empty, Permissions shows `read-write` for every file on Unix (`(None, false, false)` arm, mod.rs:180-187), and Group By Date Created puts everything under 'No Date' (crates/fffinder-core/src/grouping.rs:76-96). `wants_last_opened` looks at `config.sort`, never at `result_sort` (src/finder/list.rs:72-77).
proposal: Engine (crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs): add `sort: Option<SortOrder>` and `full_metadata: bool` to `SearchRequest` (both default off, so `/v1/find` in src/server/mod.rs:407 is unchanged). In `search()`, when `sort` is a key other than Relevance, fetch wide (`limit.max(20_000)`, the path `wide` already uses at 665-669) and, after the dedup at 585-586 and before `raw.truncate(limit)`, sort `raw` by that key: Name via `natural_cmp`, Modified and Size from `RawHit` (stat folder hits for their date), Kind via `kind::kind_label`, Folder via the parent path; for Created/LastOpened stat the candidates first. In `RawHit::into_hit` use `FileEntry::from_path` for files too when `full_metadata` is set (and `read_last_opened` when that key is wanted). UI (src/finder/mod.rs): pass `self.result_sort` and `full_metadata = result sort/group key is Created or LastOpened, or a Created/LastOpened/Permissions column is shown` in `run_search`; in `set_sort`/`set_ascending`/`set_group_by`/`toggle_column` re-run the search when searching. Keep the client-side sort in `rebuild_rows` so Keep Folders on Top still applies.
original_test_plan: Unit test in engine.rs (pattern of the tests at 1986-2045): temp dir with a.log (10 bytes), b.log (3000), c.log (200), d.log (50); `search(SearchRequest{ query: "*.log", limit: 2, sort: Some(Size descending), .. })` returns [b.log, c.log]; with `full_metadata: true` on unix `hits[0].entry.mode.is_some()`. Headless test in tests/controls.rs: write the same files into the fixture, `ui.click("view-list")`, `set_result_limit(2)`, `set_query("*.log")`, `set_sort(SortKey::Size)`; assert `ui.names() == ["b.log", "c.log"]`. Second test: `toggle_column(ListColumn::Permissions)` while searching and assert the row's `permissions()` is an `rwx` string, not `read-write`.
original_risks: A sorted search over-fetches up to 20,000 candidates per keystroke (off the UI thread, same cost as today's quoted-phrase searches); Created/LastOpened need a stat per candidate, so bound it. Sorting is still limited to what fff-search returns for the fetch size, so say 'of the first 20,000 matches' in the manual. `meta.created()` is unavailable on some Linux filesystems; tests should assert `mode` rather than `created`. Touches the same truncate site as the search-truncation-honesty and result-tie-break candidates.

verifier.claim_check:
Both defects are real, but the write-up overstates one point and the proposal has several errors.

**(1) Top-N sort: true, but "no hint" is false.**
- `Engine::search` ranks, dedups and truncates at crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs:584-587. `SearchRequest` (engine.rs:156-165) has no sort field.
- `run_search` builds the request without a sort (src/finder/mod.rs:1380-1387).
- `set_sort` / `set_ascending` only set `result_sort` and call `rebuild_rows` (mod.rs:2146-2169), which re-sorts the fetched `self.results` (mod.rs:1222-1259).
- The cap is hinted and documented: the status bar adds `+` to the count when the search hit the limit (src/finder/bars.rs:330-333), and docs/manual.md:148 and :362 describe it. The manual does not say that Sort By only reorders the capped set.
- There is precedent for over-fetching for post-processing: a Nushell filter fetches 5,000 (src/finder/filter.rs:27, mod.rs:1375-1379).

**(2) Missing metadata: true as stated.**
- File hits are built from the index with `created: None, mode: None, last_opened: None, readonly: false` (engine.rs:1384-1397). Only dir hits are stat'ed (engine.rs:1379).
- List columns render for search rows (src/finder/views.rs:897-905). So Date Created and Date Last Opened are blank, and Permissions shows `read-write` for every file hit on Unix, even a 0444 file (mod.rs:180-187).
- `compare` on Created/LastOpened ties every file and falls through to name (crates/fffinder-core/src/listing.rs:182-186).
- Group By Date Created or Date Last Opened puts every file under "No Date" (crates/fffinder-core/src/grouping.rs:76-77, 94-97); groups apply to search results (src/finder/groups.rs:123-125).
- The Sort By menu offers Date Created while searching (src/finder/toolbar.rs:551-555), and the Date Created / Date Last Opened headers are clickable sorts (crates/fffinder-core/src/config.rs:119-127).
- `wants_last_opened` reads only `config.sort` (src/finder/list.rs:72-77) and only feeds folder listings; nothing reads last-opened for results.
- `Engine::recents` goes through the same `into_hit` (engine.rs:844-850), so Recents has the same blank columns.
- Contents search already stats each hit with `FileEntry::from_path` (mod.rs:3013) and is not affected by (2).

**Errors in the proposal.**
- "/v1/find is unchanged" is wrong: src/server/mod.rs:407-414 is an exhaustive struct literal, so new `SearchRequest` fields break the build until it gets `..Default::default()`.
- `toggle_column` is `pub(super)` (list.rs:514), so the test plan cannot call it.
- Re-run sites are missing: `list_columns_changed` / `reset_list_columns` (list.rs:539-554) and `adopt_settings` (mod.rs:2352-2364, a column toggled in another tab).

No test pins the current behaviour. `search_results_sort_by_folder` (tests/columns.rs:266-292) only checks ordering of two hits and survives.
verifier.implementation_notes:
Do it as two commits. A is small and safe; B carries the risk.

**A. Metadata for result rows**
1. Add `pub fn read_metadata(&mut self)` to `FileEntry` in crates/fffinder-core/src/entry.rs, beside `read_last_opened`. It should fill only `created`, `mode` (via the private `unix_mode`), `readonly` and `is_symlink`, and leave the entry untouched if the stat fails.
2. Do not swap file hits to `FileEntry::from_path` as proposed. That would recompute `hidden` from Windows attributes (hits would vanish depending on which column is shown) and drop stale index entries, changing counts and the `+` hint.
3. Add `full_metadata: bool` and `last_opened: bool` to `SearchRequest`, both default false. Apply them in `RawHit::into_hit` (engine.rs:1376), after truncation, so at most `limit` stats.
4. Add `..Default::default()` to the literal at src/server/mod.rs:407.
5. In the UI, add `wants_result_metadata()` and `wants_result_last_opened()` next to `wants_last_opened` in src/finder/list.rs. They are true when `result_sort.key`, the active group key (`config.use_groups && config.group_by`), or a shown column is Created / Permissions / LastOpened respectively. Pass them in `run_search` (mod.rs:1380).
6. Re-run the search (`if self.is_searching() && !self.search_contents { self.run_search(false, cx) }`) when a need flips on, in:
   - `set_group_by` (src/finder/groups.rs:152)
   - `list_columns_changed` (list.rs:539), which also covers `reset_list_columns`
   - `adopt_settings` (mod.rs:2352-2364): extend the `new_data` column check to Created and Permissions

**B. Sort before the cut**
1. Add `sort: Option<SortOrder>` to `SearchRequest`. Have `run_search` pass `(result_sort.key != SortKey::Relevance).then_some(result_sort)`.
2. In `search()` (engine.rs:510), compute `sorted` and pass `wide || sorted` to `search_root` so `fetch` becomes `limit.max(20_000)` (engine.rs:665). Keep the exact-phrase `retain` and the `total_matched = raw.len()` override at engine.rs:557-565 gated on `!exact.is_empty()` only; use a separate variable, do not reuse `wide`.
3. After the dedup at engine.rs:585-586 and before `truncate`, stable-sort `raw` so relevance breaks ties, honouring `ascending` in the comparator:
   - Name: `listing::natural_cmp` on a precomputed display name (decorate-sort-undecorate; do not allocate per comparison).
   - Modified: `RawHit.modified`; stat dir hits first, since theirs is 0.
   - Size: `RawHit.size`, dirs as 0, matching `listing::compare`'s dir tiebreak.
   - Kind: `kind::kind_label` via `sort_by_cached_key`, then name.
   - Folder: `path.parent()`.
   - Created / LastOpened: do not stat 20,000 candidates per keystroke. A background search cannot be cancelled once started, and `result_sort` persists while typing. First cut `raw` to a relevance-ranked pool of `limit.max(5_000)` (same number as `FILTER_SEARCH_LIMIT`), stat that pool, sort, then truncate.
4. Return hits in sorted order. `rebuild_rows` skips the client sort when searching from Recents / Trash / Results with Name ascending (`keep_order`, mod.rs:1248-1251, does not check `is_searching`). Either rely on engine order there or add `!self.is_searching()` to `keep_order`.
5. Keep the client sort in `rebuild_rows` for Keep Folders on Top and the name tiebreak. Do not pass `folders_first` to the engine, or matching folders would crowd out files.
6. In `set_sort` and `set_ascending` (mod.rs:2146, 2161), keep the immediate `rebuild_rows`, then `run_search(false, cx)` when searching by name. Re-run on every key and direction change, including back to Relevance.

**Design pitfall to decide before coding.** Unquoted words match as a subsequence across the whole path (manual.md:356). Sorting 20,000 fuzzy candidates by size or date will lift weak path-only matches above strong name matches that relevance used to keep on top. It is exact for globs, quoted phrases and kind-only queries.
- Recommended: sort the full candidate set for every query and document it ("quote a word to sort only names that contain it").
- Fallback if that looks noisy in a real home folder: for queries with unquoted fuzzy words, sort only the relevance-top 5,000.

**Docs**
- docs/manual.md:295-303 and :358-364: a non-Relevance sort is applied to the matches (up to 20,000 per search location; 5,000 for Date Created / Date Last Opened) before the result limit.
- CHANGELOG.md, Unreleased › Fixed.

**Out of scope, worth a note:** Recents shows the same blank Created / Permissions via `into_hit`, and contents-search rows never get `last_opened`.
verifier.test_plan:
**Engine unit test** in crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs, following `quoted_words_match_names_letter_for_letter` (engine.rs:1986-2044):
- Temp dir with `a.log` (10 bytes), `b.log` (3000), `c.log` (200), `d.log` (50); `Engine::new(EngineOptions { watch: false, .. })`; `wait_ready`.
- Search with `query: "*.log"`, `files_only: true`, `limit: 2`.
- Assert both directions: Size descending gives `[b.log, c.log]` and Size ascending gives `[a.log, d.log]`. One direction alone is not discriminating, because the relevance top-2 for a glob-only query is arbitrary (frecency / mtime in whole seconds). Today both directions return the same two files, so one assertion must fail before the fix.
- With `full_metadata: true`, assert `#[cfg(unix)] hits[0].entry.mode.is_some()`. Do not assert `created`; it is unavailable on some Linux filesystems.
- Assert the default request (`sort: None`, `full_metadata: false`) still returns `mode == None`, so `/v1/find` cost is unchanged.

**Headless UI test** in tests/controls.rs (search section, near line 301), using `Fixture` and `Ui` from tests/common/mod.rs:
- Write the four `.log` files before `Ui::open`. The engine is built with `watch: false` at open (common/mod.rs:162-169); `nushell_filter_and_smart_folders` (controls.rs:1422) does the same.
- `ui.click("view-list")`, then `ui.update(|f, _, cx| f.set_result_limit(2, cx))`, `ui.update(|f, _, cx| f.set_query("*.log".into(), true, cx))`, `ui.update(|f, _, cx| f.set_sort(SortKey::Size, cx))`. `ui.update` settles.
- Assert `ui.names() == ["b.log", "c.log"]`. Then `ui.update(|f, _, cx| f.set_ascending(true, cx))` and assert `["a.log", "d.log"]`.

**Permissions column test** (same file):
- `toggle_column` is `pub(super)`, so drive the header menu as tests/file_ops.rs:915-916 does: while searching, `ui.right_click("Size"); ui.click_menu_item("Permissions");`.
- Under `#[cfg(unix)]`, assert `ui.read(|f| f.rows_for_test()[0].permissions().to_string())` starts with `rw` and is not `read-write`.
- Optionally `set_group_by(Some(GroupKey::Created))` and check `group_headers()` on a filesystem that reports birth time; skip if `std::fs::metadata(..).created()` errs.

**Regression checks to re-run:**
- tests/columns.rs `search_results_sort_by_folder` (clicking the Folder header now also re-runs the search)
- tests/controls.rs `sort_menu_items`, `list_headers_sort`, `groups_collapse_and_hide_their_items`
- tests/server.rs (the `/v1/find` literal)

I did not run cargo; the review was read-only.
verifier.risks:
- **Result quality for fuzzy queries.** Sorting 20,000 subsequence-across-path candidates by size or date can put weak path-only matches at the top, where today's "top 500 by relevance, then sort" keeps name matches. It is exact only for globs, quoted phrases and kind filters. This needs a documented rule, or a smaller relevance-ranked pool for fuzzy words.
- **Performance.** While a sort is active, every debounced keystroke runs a wide (20,000 per root) fetch plus per-hit path work, and a synchronous background search cannot be cancelled once started. One-letter and quoted searches already pay this cost. Created / LastOpened sorts need a stat (plus an xattr read on macOS) per candidate, so they must use a bounded pool. That makes those two keys cover fewer matches than Size or Modified, which the manual must say.
- **Still not exhaustive.** Results are limited to what fff-search returns for the fetch size, per root.
- **Metadata stats on slow volumes.** Up to `limit` stats per search (as many as 5,000 with a filter or a high limit) is slow on network or cold volumes; that is why it is gated on a column, sort or group actually needing it.
- **Behaviour change.** Choosing a sort now changes which items are shown, not just their order, and triggers a re-search (spinner, rows replaced; selection is remapped by path).
- **Merge conflicts.** It touches the same truncate site (engine.rs:584-587) as the search-truncation-honesty and result-tie-break candidates.
- **Build break if missed.** src/server/mod.rs:407 must be updated or the crate will not compile.

orchestrator_notes: This one changes result quality for fuzzy queries, so take the verifier's cautions seriously: keep relevance order as the default, and only change what happens when the user explicitly sorts results by another column. If the honest answer after reading the code is that a full re-sort can't be made good for fuzzy queries, do the solid parts (the blank Date Created / Last Opened / Permissions columns for results) and leave the rest out with your reasons.
